messages.subject: Figure too small in the browser
messages.subject_clean: Figure too small in the browser
messages.body_plain:
I've been using ggvis for a while to build a tool, and while it's really useful, I can't work out how to automatically resize the dynamic plot in the browser. The plot always looks like this when it launches:

 <https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/-X9dsS8ivx9k/VmUZF59WYfI/AAAAAAAADN8/AzY16uz8m7k/s1600/Screen%2BShot%2B2015-12-07%2Bat%2B4.20.38%2BPM.png>
I can stretch it out, but I'd love for it to automatically fill up the space. Does anyone know if this is possible? If I could resize more move the menu options on the left then that could do it but I'm having trouble working out how.

messages.subject: Possible bug: layer_boxplots() and categorical data
messages.subject_clean: Possible bug: layer_boxplots() and categorical data
messages.body_plain:
I'm not quite sure if layer_boxplots() is working correctly with categorical data. If you use the sample given in the help file, you may notice that the whiskers and points are offset a little, and if you change the width to something even smaller, it is quite noticeable.

Example:
mtcars %>% ggvis(~factor(cyl), ~mpg) %>% layer_boxplots(width = .4)

Produces this:

 <https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/-fqi7l4nugkM/VnHfPd9JinI/AAAAAAAATDE/HdR_LMrp9G4/s1600/bugPlot.png>

messages.subject: Possible to remove extra space at ends of axes?
messages.subject_clean: Possible to remove extra space at ends of axes?
messages.body_plain:
By default, ggvis expands the axes at either end by some factor.  When doing a stacked area chart that adds up to 100%, this can be very distracting as there will be a non-filled area around all sides.

In ggplot2, you can override this behavior by setting expand(0,0) in the axis properties.  Is this possible with ggvis directly?  Is there a viable workaround?

Thank you,
Jordan
